fr.recommendations:
• Install reflective address markers at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the single access point quickly, especially at night.
• Keep the driveway and access path clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency vehicles to reach the property without obstruction.
• Trim vegetation along the driveway edges so approaching vehicles have clear sightlines and full width of travel.
• Cut back dense plantings that may block responders from moving between the residence and other structures on foot.
• Mark any locked perimeter fence gates with reflective signage and keep them accessible with a lockbox or breakaway lock for emergency entry.
• Keep a clear turning area near the residence so emergency vehicles are not trapped with no room to reposition or exit.
• Trim shrubs and trees near the water feature to prevent hidden tripping or fall hazards for responders moving through that area at night.
• Post a property map or address placard at the entrance showing the location of all structures, the water feature, and access paths to help responders orient quickly on arrival.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree clusters closest to the structure to increase open space between the trees and the building.
• Trim branches and shrubs that are growing directly against or touching the structure.
• Separate scattered shrubs from nearby structures by removing or relocating shrubs that are immediately adjacent.
• Keep scattered trees trimmed so their branches do not connect with nearby shrubs or other trees.
• Maintain the irrigated landscape area immediately around the structure by keeping plants low-growing and well-watered.
• Remove any dead or dry plant material from within the irrigated landscape beds near the structure.
• Keep both access routes clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Mow or trim the open green space areas near the structure regularly to keep grass short.
